children: Our Bureau Mumbai: Shriram Finance, in which Japan's Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group (MUFG) has a significant stake, reported a 59.4% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to 3,677 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, driven by growth in net interest income and lower finance costs.

It reported a net profit of 2,307 crore a year earlier. Net interest margin (NIM), a measure of core profitability, improved to 9.52% from 8.19% a year earlier. "Our long-term guidance has consistently been around 8.5%, but it will take some time to return to that level. For the next two quarters, we expect NIM to remain around 9%," said Parag Sharma, MD & CEO, in an interview with ET. He attributed growth in profit to two factors. "The first was growth in business volumes, and the second was the substantial benefit from lower interest costs, which lifted net interest income," he added.

Net interest income rose 38% to 8,661 crore from 6,267 crore. The increase was driven by a 15.6% rise in interest income to 13,669 crore, while interest expenses fell 9.9% to 5,008 crore. Operating profit increased 53.3% to 6,809 crore, while the cost-to-income ratio improved to 22.52% from 27.76%. Core operating profit, which excludes other income, rose 53.5% to 6,682 crore.

The profit growth came despite a 41% increase in loan losses and provisions to 1,877 crore from 1,333 crore in the year-ago quarter. On a sequential basis, provisions rose 28.3%. Total income increased 15.8% to 13,799 crore, while profit before tax rose 58.6% to 4,932 crore. Net profit was 6.8% higher sequentially than 3,445 crore in the June quarter. Assets under management (AUM) grew 17% year on year and 4.9% sequentially to 3.29 lakh crore at the end of September. The broader vehicle and equipment portfolio stood at 2.61 lakh crore, accounting for 79.46% of total AUM.

title: Shriram Fin Q2 Net up 59%
